papers.title: QLCoder: A Query Synthesizer For Static Analysis of Security Vulnerabilities

products.budget: maximum 10 iterations per CVE and agent baseline
products.tool_permissions: Claude Code framework with CodeQL MCP/LSP and execution feedback

products.budget: maximum 10 iterations per CVE and agent baseline
products.tool_permissions: Codex CLI official tools; exact permissions not reported

task.summary: CodeQL query synthesis from CVE metadata

method.summary: CVE-grounded retrieval, AST/LSP guidance, an MCP interface, and an executable CodeQL validator that feeds back into iterative query repair.

evidence.result: QLCoder synthesizes correct queries for 53.4% of CVEs versus 10% for Claude Code-only; its query F1 is 0.70, versus 0.048 for IRIS and 0.073 for CodeQL suites.
evidence.source_location: Section 4.1 Experimental Setup; Table 2; Table 5; Appendix A
evidence.caveats: The task is CodeQL security-query synthesis, not general repository-level software engineering; GPT-5 reasoning settings differ across Codex baseline rows.

experiment.reasoning_mode: Codex GPT-5 minimal and medium; Claude Sonnet 4 not-reported
experiment.turn_budget: maximum 10 iterations per CVE and agent baseline
experiment.tool_permissions: QLCoder MCP interface exposes CodeQL LSP, retrieval, and execution feedback; baseline permissions are product defaults
experiment.baseline_config: Claude Code-only; Codex with GPT-5 minimal/medium; Gemini CLI; static-analysis baselines IRIS and CodeQL suites

papers.title: Can Language Models Discover Scaling Laws?

products.budget: Baseline budget not reported; SLDAgent uses 50 evolutionary iterations
products.tool_permissions: Native CLI agent with upstream defaults

products.budget: Baseline budget not reported; SLDAgent uses 50 evolutionary iterations

task.summary: Discover symbolic scaling laws from experimental data with executable code agents.

method.summary: Evolution-based program search jointly optimizes symbolic expressions and fitting procedures, with execution feedback and MAP-Elites selection.

evidence.result: SLDAgent reaches average R2 0.748 with GPT-5 versus 0.550 for Codex GPT-5, and improves over Claude Code rows for both Claude-Haiku-4.5 and Claude-Sonnet-4.5.
evidence.source_location: Section 4.1 Agent baselines; Table 3; Appendix B.5; Appendix D
evidence.caveats: Provider-specific rows compare SLDAgent with native agents under different harnesses; the paper reports product versions but not exact token or temperature settings.

experiment.turn_budget: 50 evolutionary iterations for SLDAgent; baseline turns not reported
experiment.tool_permissions: Native CLI agent defaults; SLDAgent uses terminal execution and verifier feedback
experiment.baseline_config: Claude Code with Claude-Haiku-4.5/Claude-Sonnet-4.5; Codex with o4-mini/GPT-5; Gemini CLI and other terminal agents

papers.title: CyberGym: Evaluating AI Agents' Real-World Cybersecurity Capabilities at Scale

products.budget: Approximately 2.0 USD per task; maximum 100 iterations
products.tool_permissions: Default Codex CLI tools in repository-level vulnerability reproduction tasks

task.summary: Generate proof-of-concept tests that reproduce real vulnerabilities in source repositories.

method.summary: A scalable vulnerability-reproduction benchmark with difficulty levels, pre/post-patch execution validation, and zero-day discovery analysis.

evidence.result: Codex CLI with GPT-4.1 is directly compared with OpenHands, EnIGMA, and Cybench agent; the union of four agents reaches 18.4% Level-1 success, exposing complementary failure modes.
evidence.source_location: Section 4 experimental evaluation; Figure 5; Appendix C Detailed Agent Settings
evidence.caveats: The Codex comparison uses a calibrated approximate cost budget and 100-iteration cap; the paper does not report a Codex CLI version or exact per-call token settings.

experiment.tool_permissions: Repository files, shell execution, and Codex CLI defaults; task-specific tool details are not reported
experiment.baseline_config: Codex CLI with GPT-4.1 compared with OpenHands, EnIGMA, and Cybench agent using the same approximate cost/iteration constraints

papers.title: DeepScientist: Advancing Frontier-Pushing Scientific Findings Progressively

products.budget: Month-long exploration on 16 H800 GPUs; Claude Code task budget not separately reported
products.tool_permissions: Sandboxed Docker repository with command-line re-execution and human inspection

task.summary: Long-horizon autonomous scientific discovery with code implementation, experiment validation, and analysis/report generation.
task.benchmark: Three frontier scientific tasks; five generated research papers and multi-week operational logs

method.summary: A three-stage hypothesis, implementation/evaluation, and analysis loop backed by persistent Findings Memory and Bayesian exploration.

evidence.result: Claude Code executes all code implementation and analysis tasks as a host component; the system reports 21 validated innovations and 60% simulated acceptance under the stated review protocol.
evidence.source_location: Section F Implementation Details; Section 4.2 Experimental Setup; Figure 4
evidence.caveats: Claude Code is a host executor rather than the paper''s comparison baseline; the scientific reasoning backbone is Gemini-2.5-pro and product-level Claude Code ablations are not reported.

experiment.time_budget: Month-long cycle; one AI text-detection run lasted 14 days
experiment.tool_permissions: Claude Code confined to a duplicated sandbox repository; independent command-line verification after completion
experiment.baseline_config: Claude-4-opus in Claude Code v1.0.53 for code execution; Gemini-2.5-pro for scientific reasoning

papers.title: DevOps-Gym: Benchmarking AI Agents in Software DevOps Cycle

products.budget: 704 tasks plus 14 end-to-end pipeline tasks; five-run stability subset uses 50 tasks
products.tool_permissions: Isolated DevOps-Gym Docker environment with terminal and DevOps-specific tools

task.summary: Evaluate coding agents across build/configuration, monitoring, issue resolving, and test generation.
task.benchmark: DevOps-Gym, 704 tasks from 30+ Java/Go projects plus 14 end-to-end pipeline tasks

method.summary: A realistic dynamic DevOps environment with standardized tool interfaces, multi-stage workflows, and stage-specific metrics.

evidence.result: Claude Code with Claude-4-Sonnet reports 51.85% build/configuration, 20.56% monitoring, 23.87% issue resolving, and 13.87% test generation success.
evidence.source_location: Section 4.1 Experimental Setup; Table 1; Appendix D.3 Table 4
evidence.caveats: The paper evaluates Claude Code as one agent framework; exact product version and per-task token budget are not reported.

experiment.time_budget: 60-second inference timeout; Docker task limits otherwise not reported
experiment.runs: 5 independent runs on a sampled 50-task subset
experiment.tool_permissions: DevOps-Gym isolated Docker containers; terminal-format tool interfaces and dynamic runtime tools
experiment.baseline_config: Claude Code, OpenHands, mini-SWE-agent, and Aider with multiple backbone models; Claude Code uses Claude-4-Sonnet

papers.title: From Assistant to Independent Developer — Are GPTs Ready for Software Development?

products.budget: 101 Android app development tasks; pass@1 evaluation
products.tool_permissions: Android project repository, Gradle build, emulator, UIAutomator tests, and compilation feedback

task.summary: Build complete Android applications from natural-language specifications and pass functional/runtime tests.
task.benchmark: AppForge, 101 software-development problems from real-world Android apps

method.summary: Formal task specifications, expert-verified UI interaction traces, automated compilation/testing, and runtime fuzz testing create a full-app benchmark.

evidence.result: Claude Code with Qwen3-Coder reaches 6.93% functional success; the paper reports that coding-agent gains are marginal and that multi-file integration and lifecycle behavior remain bottlenecks.
evidence.source_location: Section 4.3 Table 2; Appendix C.1 Setup; Appendix C.2 detailed statistics
evidence.caveats: The paper reports Claude Code as CC with Qwen3-Coder; it does not report a product version or a separate CLI iteration budget.

experiment.time_budget: 600-second fuzzing duration shown for the evaluation environment
experiment.tool_permissions: Android emulator API 31, Gradle 7.5.1, UIAutomator, compilation feedback, and runtime fuzzing
experiment.baseline_config: Claude Code and mini-SWE-agent compared with standalone LLMs on AppForge

products.budget: Up to 12 hours per task-agent-model configuration; Codex judge budget not separately reported

task.summary: Evaluate whether ML/scientific agents improve solution performance while producing methodologically novel solutions.
task.benchmark: InnoGym/iBench, 18 tasks with a 10-task main evaluation subset

method.summary: Agent-as-judge extraction and comparison turns complete solution repositories into summaries/pseudocode and scores novelty against known solutions.

evidence.result: Codex with GPT-5 is actually used as the extraction and novelty-evaluation host; the benchmark compares MLAB, CodeAct, and AIDE rather than using Codex as a primary agent baseline.
evidence.source_location: Section 3.2 Novelty Evaluation; Section 4.1; Appendix F.1
evidence.caveats: The paper calls the host product Codex rather than Codex CLI and does not report its product version or exact decoding settings; it is included as a related host use, not a direct product comparison.

experiment.time_budget: Up to 12 hours per task-agent-model configuration
experiment.runs: 3 runs for main configurations; host judge count not reported
experiment.tool_permissions: Codex reads solution repositories and emits summary.md/pseudocode.tex; novelty prompt uses GPT-5 scoring
experiment.baseline_config: MLAB, CodeAct, and AIDE are the main agent frameworks; Codex is the novelty-evaluation host

papers.title: Helmsman: Autonomous Synthesis of Federated Learning Systems via Collaborative LLM Agents

products.budget: 16 AgentFL-Bench tasks; baseline token and cost budgets are reported per task in Appendix Tables 8-12
products.runs: 3 independent runs for reported benchmark averages
products.tool_permissions: not-reported for the Claude Code baseline

products.budget: 16 AgentFL-Bench tasks; baseline token and cost budgets are reported per task in Appendix Tables 8-12
products.runs: 3 independent runs for reported benchmark averages
products.tool_permissions: not-reported for the Codex CLI baseline

task.summary: End-to-end synthesis of federated learning systems from high-level specifications.
task.benchmark: AgentFL-Bench, 16 tasks across five federated-learning research areas; cross-silo (5 clients) and cross-device (10 clients) settings

method.summary: Human-in-the-loop planning, modular code generation by collaborative agent teams, and closed-loop sandboxed evaluation and refinement with hierarchical runtime and semantic verification.

evidence.result: Claude Code with Claude Sonnet 4.5 reports 43.75% success and Codex with GPT-5.1-Codex reports 37.50%; Helmsman with Claude Sonnet 4.5 and GPT-5.1 reports 100% success in the paper's 16-task comparison.
evidence.source_location: Section 4.2 Implementation Details; Appendix A.1 Tables 8-12; Appendix A.2 Table 12; PDF p. 15
evidence.caveats: The paper compares a multi-agent federated-learning system synthesis framework against product code-synthesis baselines. CLI versions, temperature, tool permissions, and exact budget caps are not reported. Helmsman's main backbone uses Gemini-2.5-flash for planning and Claude-Sonnet-4.0 for coding and evaluation; additional experiments use Claude-Sonnet-4.5 and GPT-5.1.

experiment.turn_budget: Maximum 10 debugging attempts in Helmsman evaluation; baseline turn and iteration caps are not reported
experiment.token_budget: Appendix Tables 8-12 report per-task and average total tokens for each configuration
experiment.api_budget: Appendix Tables 8-12 report per-task and average dollar costs; no common budget cap is declared
experiment.runs: 3 independent runs for reported benchmark averages; Appendix A.2 reproducibility study
experiment.tool_permissions: Sandboxed simulation, terminal and code execution, and hierarchical runtime and semantic verification; exact Claude Code and Codex CLI permissions are not reported
experiment.baseline_config: Codex (GPT-5.1-Codex) and Claude Code (Claude Sonnet 4.5) compared with Helmsman variants and task-specific federated-learning baselines
